title: Understanding SVD
text: In Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), a matrix X is decomposed into three matrices: U, S, and $$V^T$$. The matrix S contains the singular values on its diagonal, which are crucial for determining the variance captured by each principal component.

title: Reconstruction Loss
text: Reconstruction loss refers to the difference between the original data and the data reconstructed from the principal components. If all principal components are used, the reconstruction loss should be zero.

hintAnswer: The diagonal entries of S represent the variance captured by each principal component.
title: Matrix S and Variance
text: What does the matrix S tell us about the variance captured by each principal component?
choices: The diagonal entries of S represent the variance captured by each principal component.
The diagonal entries of S represent the mean of each feature.
The diagonal entries of S represent the sum of each feature.

hintAnswer: The reconstruction loss should be zero.
title: Using All Principal Components
text: If Justin uses all three principal components, what should be the reconstruction loss?
choices: The reconstruction loss should be zero.
The reconstruction loss should be minimal but not zero.
The reconstruction loss should be significant.
